newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Polifin, AECI seen posting healthy growth.
newsitem.headline: Polifin, AECI seen posting healthy growth.

text.p: South African chemicals firms AECI Ltd and Polifin Ltd are both set to post healthy rises in profit in the next two weeks, but Polifin remains the market favourite, analysts said on Friday.

Both firms are facing uncertainty on the South African market as the industry reacts to the general slowdown in the economy. But analysts said the two groups had been exporting their basic chemical products successfully.
"The local market is a bit patchy, but you can export. Polifin has been exporting substantial quantities of polypropylene to the East," one analyst said.

Polifin is still a relatively fresh face on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, but its management has earned market respect and its bulk chemicals products have been riding high on the back of an upturn in the chemicals price cycle.
Analysts forecast a rise in earnings per share on a range of 99.6 cents to 107.0 from 83 last time. The dividend was seen edging up to a range of 33 cents to 34, from 27.
Consensus figures for the results, due to be released next Thursday, were for earnings of 102.1 cents and a dividend of 33.2.

All upstream chemical firms get a cash windfall from a cyclical upturn, but Polifin is able to reap especially good returns due to a cost-cutting feedstock relationship with one of its major shareholders, Sasol Ltd.

One analyst said Polifin was able to get margins of 20 percent, compared to the 10 percent achieved by foreign rivals like Dutch firms EVC International and DSM. "Polifin is a tremendous company, it has good margins and good management," one analyst said.

But one problem Polifin faces is that bulk chemicals have peaked and look to be heading for a downturn that is not expected to hit bottom until 1999. "People like Polifin, but there is concern about the cycle in the near-future," said Themis Themistocleous, analyst at SBC Warburg.

Analysts said the trough would be a test for the group, but its lower costs should see it cope with the price fall better than rivals. "Polifin is still going to be your preferred exposure to petrochemicals," one analyst said.

AECI, which is posting half year results on August 4, owns a 40 percent chunk of Polifin and stands to benefit from the firm's strong performance, but the group is seen as being dragged down by some of its other operations.
Analysts are predicting earnings per share in a range of 92.0-113.0 cents from 79 last time. The dividend was seen edging up to a range of 29 cents to 32, from 25.
Consensus figures for the results were for earnings of 103.4 cents and a dividend of 30.3, but analysts warned the firm was coming off a low base last year, exaggerating the size of the profit rise.
Analysts said the firm's Dulux paint operations were struggling in a market hit by the general malaise in South Africa's building and construction industry.
A routine ammonia plant shut-down at AECI's Kynoch unit had also hit problems and analysts suspect it may have cost more than the firm had budgeted for.

Another area of concern is the contribution from yarn business South African Nylon Spinners, which is facing pressure from a prices squeeze. "They are barely recovering cash costs (at SANS). I would love to see AECI get out of the business," one analyst said.
However, some analysts said AECI was addressing its problems and there were signs of a turnaround in Dulux and SANS. One analyst rated the stock a buy as a recovery play.
"I think there is going to be a good story here," he said.
